newsitem.title: UK: NWE straight-run fuel up on last week's deal.
newsitem.headline: NWE straight-run fuel up on last week's deal.

text.p: Euro low sulphur straight-run was offered a little higher on Monday, building on the strength of Friday's $110-$112 deal, traders said.
Regular low sulphur material was offered by at least one seller at $115 a tonne fob.
"I think the market is higher. Although there is not too much demand, avails are not too great," one trader said.
"It is just momentum from last week," a second trader said.
"It seems most people are offering in the $115 fob range today but it appears it will be crowded at the end of the month. You will have several cargoes in the same time period," the trader added.
Russian high sulphur straight-run was assessed a little firmer, with E-4 said to be very scarce.
M-100 was offered a touch higher, at two means +$6, with buying interest $1 to $2 lower, as demand continues for the material.
